synopsis: SplatAD, presented at CVPR 2025, reconstructs scenes from recordings using Gaussian splatting and renders both cameras and lidar; the cited research evidence is on-road [f3814, f15954]. Its lidar simulation models rolling shutter, intensity and ray dropout in real time [f4516]. Reported performance includes about one hour of training per scene on one NVIDIA A100 and rendering about an order of magnitude faster than NeRF methods [f4944, f16200, f4945]. Viewpoint changes remain a limitation: the glossary says SplatAD struggles when sensors move, while the March 2026 LiDAR-EVS preprint claims 48.6% and 47.2% lower lidar Chamfer distances than SplatAD at a 3 m lateral shift, without extracted absolute values [f16004, f4009]. A comparable method, LiHi-GS, explicitly excludes deformable objects and harsh weather, but the supplied facts do not establish those same exclusions for SplatAD or demonstrate its suitability for off-road conditions [f4517, f3814, f4516].

relations.note: Both report approximately one hour of scene training on one A100.
